- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (0.00) and prices are trending upward, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) prices when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply a 1–3% upward bias for final 7–10 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strong (≥0.3).
- When sentiment is positive but prices are falling, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days to avoid overcorrection.
